environment.description: Same EC2 instance and application code deployed behind CloudFront distribution (d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net) with an origin request policy that normalizes and validates the 'redirect_uri' query parameter at the edge. The distribution has a CloudFront Function (viewer-request trigger) named 'oauth-redirect-guard' that performs strict URL canonicalization before forwarding: it decodes percent-encoding, resolves path traversal sequences, strips userinfo components, and rejects any request to /oauth/authorize where the decoded redirect_uri hostname does not EXACTLY match entries in an edge-side allowlist (not suffix-match). Additionally, the authorization server (auth.internal.corp) is configured with a registered redirect_uri allowlist that requires exact-match validation per RFC 6749 Section 3.1.2.2. The CloudFront distribution also enforces all script resources served through it carry SRI validation headers via a response headers policy (Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy with require-sri-for directive), meaning even if an attacker could redirect to a controlled page within the CDN origin, injected scripts without valid integrity attributes would be blocked by the CSP require-sri-for enforcement at the browser level.

config.response_headers_policy: content-security-policy: require-sri-for script style; script-src 'self' https://cdn.internal.corp
